figures.caption: Figure 2. Excerpt of one S2B-LM supporting-phase game illustrating the verbalizer’s sync-summary → inverse-prediction → match-comparison reasoning chain. Full conversation in Figure 4 (Appendix B).
Figure 3. Empirical scatter of adj-ZSCT against miniF2F accuracy. The adj-ZSCT axis captures structured receptive CLB capability adjusted above the 50% random-guessing baseline.

Table 2. Evaluation results: adj-ZSCT (S2B-LM receptive listener CLB competency, ability above chance) and miniF2F whole-proof test-split accuracy (Pass@32). ZSCT scores reported as mean ± std. err. over 8 random seeds. †: model accessed via API.

Figure 4. S2B-LM conversation examples over 6 supporting-phase games illustrating the hypothesis-tracking rule-based listener verbalizer. System sets the task context. User messages present each game’s stimulus and message, followed by the sync-step revelation of the speaker’s target. Listener responses are produced by VERBALIZE (Algorithm 1): game #0 defaults to same (no sync data yet); subsequent games accumulate sync-derived token-to-value evidence in V and apply the sync-summary → inverse-prediction → match-comparison chain; games #3–#5 illustrate how the evidence base grows across episodes, with partial matches (1/3, 2/3) correctly classified as different even as the mapping fills in.
